title: SPARC Cat - Sham Control Chronic Cat 3 Day 30
author: Brett Hanzlicek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfzyjp7w
materials: Transport cat from housing site to surgery site.

steps.title: Prepare Animal for Surgery
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the cat and prepare the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Move the cat to the surgery room and attach monitors.
Drape the animal and perform a betadine scrub on the abdomen and genitals.

steps.title: Insert Bladder Catheter
steps.instruction: Place a 3.5Fr catheter into the bladder via the urethra.

substeps.instruction: Insert the catheter into the bladder through the urethra.
Advance the catheter until resistance is met, then pull back 2-3 cm.

steps.title: Collect Urine Sample
steps.instruction: Withdraw urine from the bladder using gentle suction with a syringe.

substeps.instruction: Measure the volume of the withdrawn urine (e.g., 18 mL).

steps.title: Perform Contrast Imaging
steps.instruction: Visualize the bladder using a 1:5 dilution of contrast to saline.

substeps.instruction: Fill the bladder with 10 mL contrast and take a single image.
Add 10 mL more (total 20 mL) and take a single image.
Add 5 mL more (total 25 mL) and take a single image.
Take a 3D CT image with 25 mL contrast:saline in the bladder.

steps.title: Set Up Cystometry Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the pressure recording system after transferring the cat from isoflurane to propofol anesthetic.

substeps.instruction: Set up a syringe pump with a fill rate of 2 mL saline/minute.
Connect an external pressure transducer between the syringe pump and the tubing leading to the catheter.
Configure Labview software to record the pressure data.

steps.title: Perform Urodynamics Recording
steps.instruction: Fill the bladder with saline and record the pressure via the transducer and LabView.

substeps.instruction: Fill the bladder with saline at a rate of 2 mL/min.
Fill to 20 mL and record pressure.
Remove the bladder and examine it.
Place the bladder in formalin for histological analysis.
